answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake before it can act as a vertex in the transaction graph. Like a single drop cannot claim to be an ocean, one operator cannot cheaply multiply identities: each new identity demands fresh capital locked for a fixed period. If an agent cheats, the stake is slashed and its reputation is crystal clear to peers, so the cost of forging many identities grows linearly while honest agents pay only once.
